ext.codex.call.config_unreadable: [codex-call] could not read config, using defaults: {error}
ext.codex.call.cwd_help: working directory for codex (default: current directory)
ext.codex.call.cwd_missing: [codex-call] failed: working directory does not exist: {cwd}
ext.codex.call.description: codex-call.py: hands a prompt to `codex exec` and returns the answer or a clear failure. The single entry point this system uses to call Codex (the acceptance judge's assessor goes through it too).
ext.codex.call.model_help: model slug (default: codex_companion.model; if unset, codex's own default)
ext.codex.call.no_answer: codex gave no answer (both the -o file and stdout are empty)
ext.codex.call.timeout_help: time limit in seconds, killed on timeout (default {default})
ext.codex.companion.disabled: [Codex Companion] Disabled: {reason}. Effect: the acceptance judge (AI reviewing AI), plan review and handoff self-check will not run; local heuristic soft gates and the other guardian mechanisms work normally. To enable it, install the codex CLI or make sure the claude CLI can be found (fallback judge). This message appears only once per machine.
ext.codex.companion.fallback_reminder: [Codex Companion reminder] The last review got no valid response, so this turn falls back to heuristics-only. Sources: {sources}
ext.codex.companion.self_check_advice: Check the gaps listed above yourself: if something really was missed, add the verification or fix in this turn; ignore false alarms.
ext.codex.companion.self_check_summary: Closing self-check found {count} high-risk gaps (does not block closing)
ext.codex.judge.codex_not_entitled: codex is not entitled or its quota is limited: {reason}
ext.codex.judge.no_fallback_cli: and no claude CLI was found to act as the fallback judge
ext.codex.run.codex_failed: [codex-run] codex did not complete: {reason}; codex's stderr is in {stderr_file}
ext.codex.run.cwd_help: review: the repo to review; build: the dedicated working tree
ext.codex.run.description: codex-run.py: builds the Codex prompt per the codex skill, runs it in the right sandbox, compares VCS status before and after, and saves the raw output in full.
ext.codex.run.guard_changed: [codex-run] warning: the VCS status of {path} differs before and after the run; see {out_dir}/guard-before-*.txt and guard-after-*.txt
ext.codex.run.guard_help: a directory that must not change across the run; can be given more than once
ext.codex.run.identity_missing: [codex-run] warning: {identity} does not exist, so section 2 is missing "{section}"
ext.codex.run.new_help: build the prompt skeleton (section 2 pastes the user's rulers automatically)
ext.codex.run.out_dir_help: output, stderr and before/after status are saved here
ext.codex.run.refuse_build_without_guard: [codex-run] refusing to run: build mode needs --guard <live repo>, otherwise the run cannot tell whether live was touched
ext.codex.run.refuse_cwd_missing: [codex-run] refusing to run: --cwd does not exist: {cwd}
ext.codex.run.refuse_unfilled: [codex-run] refusing to run: {prompt_file} still has {count} unfilled "{mark}" places
ext.codex.run.run_help: check, run codex in a sandbox, save the output, and compare the before/after status
ext.codex.run.sandbox_help: use workspace-write only when the read-only sandbox cannot start and you review a temp copy instead; danger-full-access is not offered
ext.codex.run.section_missing: [codex-run] failed: {path} has no "## {heading}" section (was the heading renamed?)
ext.codex.run.timeout_help: time limit in seconds (default 1800; Codex reads the repo itself, so 300 is often not enough)
